How to Evaluate a Buyer Offer

Turn an offer notification into a calm, repeatable decision.

An offer is worth evaluating against the economics of the offered price—not the original list price. Recalculate percentage fees, then subtract item cost, shipping, preparation, and other expenses.

Set the floor before negotiating

Choose either a minimum dollar profit or a minimum ROI. If an offer misses that target, calculate the counteroffer needed to reach it instead of responding from memory.

The offer calculator labels the estimate as meeting or missing your selected threshold and shows the gap. That language supports a decision; it does not promise the sale will be profitable.

Consider non-financial factors

Time in inventory, storage pressure, return risk, and confidence in your cost estimate may justify a different choice. Keep the calculation visible so the tradeoff is deliberate.

Keep the estimate honest.

Fee structures and actual costs can change. Verify the rules that apply to your sale and treat every result as planning information.
